title: Qcqs geometric exchange factors through strict-local sections
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ give a cartesian square with $f,s$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Put $R=\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,s}$ and $\rho:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ as the affine-neighbourhood colimit and structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put $Z=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}R$, with projections $p:Z\to X$ and $h:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $H=p^{-1}F$. There exist a local-ring structure on R making it strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], a geometric closed point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $q:X'\to Z$ with a cartesian square $(q,f',h,t)$ and $pq=g'$, together with an isomorphism $e:(f_*F)_s\simeq\Gamma(Z,H)$. On the identity geometric stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the specified exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is the composite of the inverse-image stalk isomorphism, $e$, restriction $\Gamma(Z,H)\to\Gamma(X',q^{-1}H)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback], the composition identification $q^{-1}p^{-1}F\simeq g'^{-1}F$, the inverse global-sections pushforward identification, and the terminal-neighbourhood germ. No properness or invertibility of the middle restriction is asserted. The terminal germ is the real global-sections identification followed by toPresheafFiber at the identity object, and is invertible.
